answers: Nothing — two awaits already overlap by default
They run one after the other, so the waits add up
await cannot appear twice in one function
writing.exampleCaption: join overlaps the waits instead of adding them up.
writing.explanation: join runs futures at the same time and waits for all of them; select takes whichever finishes first. Dropping a future cancels it at its last await point, which is a real advantage over threads — but it means anything that must not be interrupted needs to be written with that in mind.
writing.feedback: Sequential awaits serialise work that could have overlapped.
